title: Help with my bot
author: Academic-Tear381
selftext: Im currently using Claude ai coding to build an ai trading bot with a sort of starter pack  i found on github through insta but i had troubles for over 2 hours trying to connect to the paper trading site which is alpaca but now i cannot get my bot to buy or sell without my permission and i was wondering should the final result be its own app? So i can moniter everything without claude?, any advice would be greatly appreciated 🙏

comments.author: tylenol_and_crayons
comments.body: Youve got a lot to work on my friend

comments.author: QuanTradin
comments.body:
that permission box is Claude asking before it runs each command, so right now Claude is the one pressing buy. yes, make it its own program: one python file on a timer that sends the Alpaca paper orders itself and logs each one. Claude writes the file, you start it.

if the wiring keeps eating evenings, Quantradin skips it. I built it earlier this year: plug Claude in and it trades stocks with pretend money, every order on one page. quantradin.com. is the bot a file you can run on your own yet?

comments.author: escopetadoce
comments.body:
Everything that you just wrote here you can feed to Claude  
\> make an independent app  
\> trade for me

That's what Claude is for: you tell it what you want and it will return what you asked. I don't see the problem.

Tell Claude to look  at the repository, test it out to see if it works; check if there's any security issue that you should be concern and iif it's safe, then ask it to build you a trading strategy that buys and sell base on the signal rules from that repository.

If you can't express in words what you want to do and send it to Claude, then you should quit now before you lose money.

comments.author: ditchtheworkweek
comments.body: I have created several bots. Several folks have asked me to create a Substack that can help people to create bots using best developer methods with ai coding assistance. Is this something that anyone would find interesting? I personally think it’s harder than most are willing to stick with it to get a fully functional trading bot. To short answer to your question is use their alpaca rest api. Create an engine in python that manages your trades. Having Claude make trades will not work the way you want it too.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: A few thoughts. If the bot asks for approval before each trade, that's often a setting in the starter code, so look for a flag or a confirm step in the order function. The prompts could also be coming from Claude Code asking permission for each command, which is a separate thing from the bot itself. For monitoring, you don't need a full app: a simple log file or a small dashboard that shows positions, orders and errors is enough to start. Since the code came from a starter pack found on Instagram, I'd read through it before giving it any keys, keep it on paper trading, and put hard limits on order size in the code.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body:
Yes, make it its own script. The bot shouldn't depend on any chat window staying open. A plain Python script that runs on a schedule (cron on Linux, Task Scheduler on Windows, or a small cloud server) is enough for Alpaca paper trading.

  
For the connection problem, first check that you're using the paper API keys together with the paper base URL, not the live one. Mixing them gives an auth error that looks like the whole bot is broken.

  
For monitoring, have it write every order, fill and error to a log file, or send you a message when something fails. That tells you much more than watching it run.

comments.author: eduard_trades
comments.body:
Yes, it should be its own program. Claude asks for permission because it's running the commands itself, and that's a good thing: you don't want an AI session with standing permission to place orders.



The setup that works for me: Claude writes the code, but the bot is a plain script that runs on its own, on a schedule or in a loop. It reads prices, applies your rules, places orders through the Alpaca API with your paper keys, and writes every decision to a log file. Claude isn't involved while it runs. For monitoring, Alpaca's own dashboard already shows paper positions and orders, so you don't need to build an app yet. The log file plus that dashboard is enough to start.



Before it runs on its own, put hard limits in the code itself: max position size, max loss per day after which it stops trading, and a check that it's using the paper URL. The bot should stop itself before anything else has to.



And one thing about the starter pack: read through it before you put your keys in. Check where the keys go and whether the code sends anything to a server other than Alpaca. Keep keys in a .env file, never in the code, and never in anything you push to GitHub.

replies.author: BombardiroMateusz
replies.body: Spot on, every bot needs its own script. I trade via pu prime myself, but keep my python automation running on a separate server so chat windows don't have to stay open

comments.author: Bubblekrash
comments.body: Separate Claude from your bot and strategy unless you're using it for every trading decision. Learn Python—at least the basics. Vibe coding or asking an LLM to make you money won't get you far. Claude AI runs in a sandbox, so you'll need to move your bot to your local machine or a server like EC2 to connect to exchanges with your API keys. Good luck, and don't forget who you're competing with for liquidity.

comments.body: Upload your py code into GitHub and set it up with railway*com instead of using Claude for execution

comments.author: koryuken
comments.body: Don't get anything from guthub. Download historical data and start backtesting and looking for a strategy. Use claude code and have it build everything for you, it's trivial. At least you'll know what you're building and exactly what is happening.
